name: Framework Compare

first-party.description: Built into the framework and documented as stable.

experimental.description: Built in, but behind an experimental flag or marked unstable.

third-party.description: Available through a plugin or package the framework does not ship.

manual.description: Not built in and no package for it; you write it yourself.

labelRules: A label describes what the framework offers, not what a Books port chose. If the framework ships the feature, the cell is 1st-party even where a port wired it by hand.
Opt-in counts the same as on by default. An official package from the framework team counts as 1st-party: @nuxt/image, @sveltejs/enhanced-img and next/image all score the same.

Third-party means a community package or a host service provides the feature itself, not a building block the app still has to assemble. The cell names the package. Partytown counts only where the framework's own docs point to it.
Manual means nothing covers it. The app wires it by hand or goes without.
Every cell links the vendor docs behind its label. For Manual and Third-party cells, that is the docs page on the topic, which documents no first-party option.
